title: cedar-bay-returns-assistant-onramp-notes
content:
High-level context:
Cedar Bay (mid-market omnichannel retailer) wants a Returns Assistant to speed up in-store and online returns. Goal: 40% faster agent handling time + 25% fewer manual lookups. They require private deployment (on-premise or VPC-hosted) due to cardholder data and regional privacy rules.

Call notes (2025-01-14 discovery):
- Attendees: Maya P. (Redwood CS), Ravi K. (Redwood Solutions), Ava M. (Cedar Bay Product), Liam O. (Cedar Bay SRE), Charlotte W. (Redwood Solutions)
- Primary flows discussed:
  1) In-store agent assistant: agent scans receipt barcode or uploads photo -> OCR -> assistant extracts order id, validates purchase -> suggests return reason, policy, and pre-authorizes refund.
  2) Online self-service: customer uploads receipt/email or enters order id -> assistant confirms eligibility, auto-populates return label steps, or escalates to live agent.
  3) Fraud/exception path: if mismatch or high-risk flags, route to canary model or human review.
- Non-negotiables:
  - No PII or PAN storage outside customer-controlled environment (KMS/HSM requirement)
  - SLA: sub-300ms median inference for agent flow (agent-facing); 500-800ms acceptable for customer-facing web flow
  - Audit logs for every inference (hash of input + model version + route) retained for 180 days

Technical requirements / constraints:
- Private deployment: Redwood Private in their VPC preferred; on-prem option if egress/network restrictions block cloud control plane.
- OCR: Cedar Bay uses ABBYY in-store legacy pipeline sending extracted text to Redwood. We should support both raw images and OCR text input to be resilient.
- Models: smaller LLM for structured extraction + mid-size assistant model for reasoning and policy logic. Consider splitting: image/text extraction -> structured form -> embedding lookup + retrieval -> generation.
- Embeddings: product catalog (1.2M skus) must be sharded and served via a vector DB in-customer VPC; Redwood can host embedding compute but index must remain in-customer network.
- Token budget: typical receipt + context ~ 600-900 tokens; plus transient policy and product context ~ up to 1.5k tokens. Need to enforce prompt trimming and leverage prefix caching for repeated customers.
- Throughput estimate: peak in-store windows produce ~120 reqs/min per store; pilot 10 stores -> 1,200 reqs/min. Agent-fast path requires small batching (1-4) with auto-scaling burst capacity.
- Hardware: recommend reserved A10G for cost pilots; H100 for highest throughput if they do heavy vector search + long-context models. Quantization recommended for assistant model (INT8/4) to reduce footprint.

Gotchas / risks surfaced:
- OCR failure modes: poor lighting / crumpled receipts -> need structured fallback: lookup by phone + date window. This increases context and tokens, pushing latency.
- PCI-scope creep: if agents paste full PAN for troubleshooting, they may expand PCI scope. Need agent UI controls + redaction middleware.
- Catalog drift: product titles in catalog often differ from receipt text -> fuzzy matching must be robust; plan for retraining/relabeling heuristics.
- Vector DB placement: customer insists index must not leave VPC; this complicates Redwood Optimize suggestions that assume hosted index.
- Rollback plan: when we introduce model rollouts, must have automatic fallback to a deterministic rules engine for returns to avoid denial-of-service on regressions.

Proposed initial architecture (sketch):
- Ingest layer in Cedar Bay VPC (NLB) -> Redwood Private edge component (in-VPC) -> preprocessing (OCR verification / redaction) -> lightweight extractor LLM (quantized) -> retrieval against product index (in-VPC vector DB) -> assistant model for decision + human readable steps -> audit log and KMS-wrapped artifacts -> response to agent UI or web client.

Acceptance criteria for pilot:
- 90th percentile agent path latency <= 400ms at 1k reqs/min sustained for 10 minutes
- Extraction accuracy (order id, amount, sku) >= 98% on sampled receipts (n=500)
- No plaintext PAN or unmasked customer identifiers written to Redwood-hosted logs
- Canary rollout mechanism validated: 10% traffic -> 50% -> rollback automated on quality/regression alert

Rough cost / capacity sketch (back-of-envelope):
- Pilot (10 stores): requirement ~ 1 A10G reserved; autoscale to 2 for bursts. Monthly infra estimate $4.5k-6k + Redwood Private licensing stub ~$3k
- Production (100 stores): baseline 6-8 A10G equivalent or 2 H100 depending on batching; monthly infra estimate $25k-$40k + licensing/support. These are placeholders; we will run perf bench with their receipts.

Open questions we need to resolve (owners):
- Can Cedar Bay accept KMS integration with Redwood control plane or do they require customer-managed HSM? (Owner: Ravi)
- Confirm retention windows for logs and whether they need SAS-70 style attestation for auditors. (Owner: Ava)
- Which POS vendors must we integrate with for webhook order lookup? (Owner: Liam)
- Vector DB choice: Pinecone (hosted) vs. in-house Milvus on their infra. They require in-VPC, so evaluate costs. (Owner: Charlotte)

Immediate next steps / action items:
- [Maya] Draft architecture diagram and send to Cedar Bay for review (due 2025-01-20) — Confluence draft link in linked_artifacts.
- [Ravi] Confirm KMS/HSM options and produce short doc on tradeoffs (due 2025-01-22) — create JIRA-RET-330.
- [Charlotte] Run rough perf sim with sample receipt set (n=2k) on local A10G to estimate token/time distribution (due 2025-01-28).
- [Ava/Cedar Bay] Provide sample receipts (redacted) and list of POS vendors (due 2025-01-18).
- Schedule follow-up technical deep-dive with infra and security (target week of 2025-01-27).

Notes to self / messy brainstorm fragments:
- Could use prefix cache for frequent order lookup responses (common returns like store credit flows) -> saves 30-60ms maybe.
- Consider a tiny on-device rules engine in the POS to short-circuit trivial returns (<= $20, no receipt).
- Need UI hook for "send to human" that includes model version + similarity score and raw OCR snapshot.
- If they insist on no outbound connections for sensitive ops, explore fully air-gapped private package (longer lead).

End of scratchpad.
summary: Scratchpad for Cedar Bay returns assistant pilot: discovery notes, constraints, architecture sketch, risks, estimates, owners and immediate next steps.
